extracted.intended_audience: general comedy fans and Ranker site voters (people ranking/reading lists of comedians)
extracted.subtask_description: Creating or voting on a ranked list of stand-up comedians who died before they had finished their careers, prioritizing those who 'left the most great comedy behind.' Intended for readers to vote on who was taken too soon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion rule: stand-up comics only (no actors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand Up Comics Who Died Before They Were Done only. (No Actors.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only performers whose primary work is stand-up comedy and who died before their career was complete should be included. Actors who are primarily known for acting (rather than stand-up) are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting criterion: upvote those who 'left the most great comedy behind'
rubrics_metrics.description: Upvote the comedians who left the most great comedy behind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voters should consider the amount and quality of comedy the performer produced and the sense that they were taken before their work was finished—i.e., potential for more great material. The page frames this as a tribute to performers who 'died too young' and emphasizes legacy and the lost future output (examples cited include Robin Williams and John Candy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking/display metric: votes and upvote rate determine placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry shows number of votes, number of voters, and an upvote rate (e.g., 'Ranked #1 by 1,455 voters with an 81% upvote rate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list's ordering is driven by community voting metrics (total votes/voters and upvote percentage). Readers should expect rank to reflect aggregate voter preferences rather than an editorial scoring rubric. Use these displayed metrics to compare perceived consensus about how much each comedian 'left behind.'
